question: how can i participate in the Auction Market?

answers: I do not have specific information on how you can participate  in the Auction Market, but in order to participate in a Dealer Market, you must be designated a Market Maker. They are dedicated to providing liquidity for the Auction Market in certain securities and therefore require that they have on hand a suitable supply of those securities which they support. If Market Makers are generally holding low quantities of a particular security, this will drive up the price in both the Dealer Market and the Auction Market. Similarly, if Market Makers are generally holding too much of a particular security, this may drive down prices on both the Auction Market and the Dealer Market."

history.content: Do brokers execute every trade on the exchange?

Brokers traditional role is to arrange the buying and selling of stock by finding buyers and sellers at an agreed upon price. They do not necessarily execute every trade on the exchange. But a trader is one who purchases stock with the hope of selling it for a gain. The trader will use a broker to help with the purchase and sale of a stock.    brokers may also buy and sell stocks for their own account that is called broker-delaer firm.

They have to be registered with FINRA and the SEC , which have their own databases for you to look up individuals and companies. You need to find out if are also acting as a consumer bank, such as how Merrill Lynch is now part of Bank of America and the accounts can be linked pretty easily, then they should will also be regulated by the FDIC. A Market maker is s someone that is contractually bound, by the exchange, to provide both bid and ask prices for a given volume. T also could be a company which will agree to partner with you to complete the sale at a set price. It is important to note that a broker can be a market maker (or work for one), also, in which case he would sell you directly the shares from the market maker reservoir.

The Auction Market is a market where investors, including Market Makers, buy and sell securities. It operates with the familiar bid-ask pricing that you see on financial pages such as Google and Yahoo. Market Makers are institutions that provide liquidity for investors to easily buy and sell shares at a fair price. They need to have a suitable supply of shares to meet investor demands. When Market Makers feel the need to quickly increase or decrease their supply of a particular security, they turn to the Dealer Market. The Auction Market and the Dealer Market both operate on a bid-ask basis, with the bid-ask prices quoted on the Dealer Market being more or less identical to those on the Auction Market, except the quote sizes will be generally much larger.
